issue.title: Bug:Debian 13 automatic delete /tmp/ folder content after 10 days

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

on Debian 13, the new default behavior is for files in /tmp/ to be automatically deleted after 10 days from the time they were last used. Files in /var/tmp are deleted after 30 days.

this behavior affect any component that uses tmp folder and needs the files for more than 10 days.

### Steps to Reproduce

on switch that have uptime of 10 days, it will trigger it automatically (or trigger manually systemd-tmpfiles --clean instead of waiting)

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**actual behavior:**
the content of /tmp/ is being removed
**expected behavior:**
/tmp/ content should stay without being deleted.

resolution.title: Prevent auto deletion of tmp and var/tmp files
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
Debian 13 enabled the upstream systemd-tmpfiles periodic cleanup, which deletes /tmp entries older than 10 days and /var/tmp after 30 days.

fixes #29395

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Ship `/etc/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf` in the image with a - on aging column:

```
q	/tmp 1777 root root -
q	/var/tmp 1777 root root -
```

#### How to verify it

```bash
# Create file on /tmp folder
touch /tmp/TestFile

# trigger the cleanup itself
systemd-tmpfiles --clean
```
